explanation: In Turkey, the OK hand sign (thumb and index finger forming a circle) is not reliably read as 'okay'; it is traditionally a vulgar gesture used as a homophobic insult. Many Turks, especially younger people in cities, also know the Western 'OK' meaning, but the gesture still carries a real risk of offending.
local_tip: Avoid using the OK hand sign entirely in Turkey; instead, nod your head or say 'tamam' (okay) to convey agreement.
regional_note: The insulting reading is most familiar to older and more traditional Turks; younger, urban people are more likely to also recognise the Western 'OK' meaning.

also_check.note: Considered a very offensive gesture, similar to an obscene insult.
Commonly used to mean 'okay' or 'good,' though some younger people may use it ironically.
Widely used to mean 'OK' or 'money,' with no negative connotations.
